slides.name: Conceptual proof loop
slides.notes: Describe this as a conceptual model, not a documented Numina Prover implementation. Candidate proof steps are checked by a formal verifier. A failed check feeds back into revision; an accepted proof proceeds. The resource budget is a proposed control over time, compute, or attempts. Emphasize that formal acceptance is distinct from explanation quality: persuasive prose cannot make an invalid step valid.

slides.name: Limits and next study
slides.notes: The toy evaluation cannot support conclusions about real-world performance. Its limitations include the small sample, invented assessors, untested distributions, absent uncertainty estimates, and possible rubric bias. A credible next step is to preregister a real study on actual theorem sets, recruit independent assessors, log verifier acceptance, measure resource use, and report uncertainty before making superiority claims.
